summary: Pemba Airport (PMA) is a regional airport serving Pemba Island, the northernmost major island in Tanzania's Zanzibar Archipelago. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting the island to Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar, and other Tanzanian cities, serving both local residents and tourists drawn to the island's spice farms, clove plantations, and world-class diving sites. The airport is located near Chake Chake, the island's main town and administrative capital, providing a vital link for this relatively remote and less-developed island compared to its famous neighbor, Unguja.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Pemba Airport?
A: Coastal Aviation and Auric Air are the main carriers serving Pemba, with regular flights to and from Zanzibar and Dar es Salaam.

Q: How far is the airport from Chake Chake?
A: Pemba Airport is located just a few kilometers east of Chake Chake town center, typically a 10 to 15 minute drive.

Q: Do I need a visa to fly into Pemba Airport?
A: Pemba is part of Tanzania, so standard Tanzanian visa requirements apply. Most visitors arrive with a tourist visa obtained in advance or on arrival at a major entry point.

Q: Is the airport suitable for international flights?
A: No, Pemba Airport handles only domestic flights. International travelers typically fly into Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar es Salaam or Abeid Amani Karume International Airport in Zanzibar first.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged hotel transfers are the most reliable ways to reach Chake Chake or other parts of the island from Pemba Airport, as public transport options are limited. Roads on Pemba can be rough and poorly lit at night, so arranging pickup in advance is strongly recommended. Many dive resorts and eco-lodges offer shuttle services that should be confirmed before arrival.
local_tip: Bring cash in Tanzanian shillings or US dollars, as card payment facilities at and around the airport are unreliable, and ATMs on the island can be scarce outside of Chake Chake town.
